gold_notes: Fourth-quarter column of the 'Product revenue' row in the Quarterly Financial Data (unaudited) note of Biogen, Inc.'s 1996 annual report, the document that reports the quarter as current (Biogen, Inc. issued no 10-Q for a fourth quarter). The quarter's first three columns match the 10-Qs. Biogen, Inc. (CIK 714655, the original Avonex owner, merged into IDEC Pharmaceuticals in November 2003) income-statement product revenue line. Biogen, Inc. had no other marketed product until AMEVIVE in 2003; its 10-Qs from 1999 to 2002 state that the Company currently derives product revenues from sales of AVONEX, and the 10-K text gives AVONEX revenues of $240.0 million (1997), $394.9 million (1998), $620.6 million (1999), $761.1 million (2000) and about $1,034.4 million (2002), each matching this line's full year. Worldwide (U.S. plus Europe and other markets from the 1997 EU launch). Fiscal year equals calendar year. Caveat for 1996: the same 10-K states 1996 AVONEX revenues of approximately $76.5 million against 78,202 on this line, and the 1996Q2 and 1996Q3 10-Qs give AVONEX sales of $6.1 and $33.6 million (six weeks and nine months), matching the line; so about $1.7 million of 1996Q4 product revenue is not identified as AVONEX in any document read.
reviewed_anomaly: Biogen, Inc.'s 1996 10-K prints Product revenue 44,560 thousand for the fourth quarter (78,202 for the year) but states twice that 1996 AVONEX revenues were approximately $76.5 million; the 1996Q2 and 1996Q3 10-Qs put AVONEX at $6.1 and $33.6 million (quarter and nine months), equal to the product line. About $1.7 million of 1996Q4 product revenue is therefore not identified as AVONEX, and no document read (1996 10-K, 1997 and 1998 10-Ks, 1997 10-Qs) says what it is. The figure as printed is kept; the AVONEX-only quarter would be about 42.9.

gold_notes: The third-quarter 2014 earnings release (accession 0001104659-14-073810) does not print Keytruda sales (the product is not on its sales table; its text reports the 4 September 2014 FDA approval and first shipments only). The fourth-quarter and full-year 2014 release prints Keytruda's four 2014 quarters as separate columns of the same sales table: 0, 0, 4, 50 and a full year of 55 (the printed full year is one more than the quarters' sum, a rounding difference). The third quarter of 2014 is the 3Q column of that row (the third of the four quarterly columns). Merck's quarterly earnings release (8-K exhibit 99.1) prints this product on its own 'Keytruda' line of the multi-column sales table (worldwide sales, USD millions, no regional split; columns are the current-year quarters and year-to-date, then the prior-year quarters, then percentage changes). The line is Merck's worldwide sales of Keytruda (pembrolizumab) and carries no footnote adding other products. From the fourth-quarter 2025 release Merck prints the intravenous product on a 'Keytruda' line and the subcutaneous product on a separate 'Keytruda Qlex' line, and the summary table headline becomes 'KEYTRUDA/KEYTRUDA QLEX'; this series is the 'Keytruda' line only, whose earlier values are unchanged, and it excludes Keytruda Qlex sales.

gold_notes: PRO FORMA, NOT AN ISSUER-REPORTED ACTUAL. Exhibit 99.2 (Certain Supplemental Information) to BMS's fourth-quarter 2019 earnings 8-K prints a worldwide pro forma quarterly trend table in which the 2019 fourth-quarter column combines Celgene's REVLIMID revenue for Oct 1 - Nov 19, 2019 with BMS's own post-acquisition revenue from Nov 20, 2019. gold_notes: J&J states this product on its own line of the Major Pharmaceutical Product Revenues table in its Form 10-Q. Each 10-Q prints two of these tables - the fiscal year to date and the fiscal quarter on its own - and the quarter is read from the second, so no arithmetic is needed. A fourth quarter is never filed as a quarter, and is the 10-K's full year less the nine months the third-quarter 10-Q states. The table first appears in the first-quarter 2005 10-Q; before that the 10-Qs name products only in prose and state no product-level figures at all.

gold_notes: Lilly's revenue from the Trajenta (linagliptin) product family under its collaboration with Boehringer Ingelheim - collaboration and other revenue, not Lilly's own product sales: Boehringer Ingelheim (private) books the product sales and Lilly prints only its own revenue line. Lilly's footnote to the line in the release product tables states 'Trajenta includes Jentadueto'. Worldwide (U.S. plus outside U.S.), USD millions as printed to a tenth of a million. A fourth quarter is never filed as a quarter, and is the 10-K's full year less the nine months the third-quarter 10-Q states.
